author: Tampa Bay Times
title: Doc Ford's Jungle Terrace location closing, changing name, then reopening - NewsBreak
text:
6 hours ago General manager Dustin Rickards, 41, said most of the menu will stay the same after the restaurant’s rebrand to Boca Ciega Waterfront Bar & Grill. [ LUCY GLYNN | Lucy Glynn ] Doc Ford’s Rum Bar & Grille in Jungle Terrace is rebranding.
The waterfront restaurant announced in a July 28 Facebook post that it will close under its original name Aug. 2. The general manager, Dustin Rickards, said that after a remodel, it will reopen as Boca Ciega Waterfront Bar & Grill on Aug. 10.
“Nothing’s changing except for the name, some decorations on the inside and just a few small menu changes,” Rickards said.
Doc Ford’s has two St. Petersburg locations. The Jungle Terrace restaurant opened December 2022, second to the St. Pete Pier spot. Rickards, 41, said recurring customer confusion between locations was a major motivator for the renaming.
“It’s something we’ve actually talked about doing for a little while,” he said. “We’ll have half a reservation show up here, half of them show up downtown. People call here and place to-go orders, and they think they’re calling the Pier location.”
The rebranding includes limited menu changes and a fresh coat of interior paint paired with new wallpaper. After the week of revamping and a new sign out front, Boca Ciega Waterfront Bar & Grill will open Aug 10.
Customers who were spooked by the social media announcement, worried their beloved dishes were leaving, don’t need to panic. The restaurant’s signature Yucatan shrimp and dry-rubbed ribeye are staying on the menu.
“We’re just closing for a week to do a couple menu changes,” Rickards said. ”Eighty percent of the menu is going to be the same, maybe 90%.”
The restaurant also plans to bring a few of its popular rotating nightly dinner specials to the fixed menu, including the crab-stuffed grouper and shrimp scampi pasta. The shrimp burger, popular at the Doc Ford’s restaurant in Fort Myers, will also be among the additions served at the newly-named Boca Ciega Waterfront Bar & Grill.
“There’s just a few things that are coming off, a couple appetizers, a couple entrees,” he said. “We’re still kind of finalizing that, though.”
Doc Ford’s Rum Bar & Grille has four total locations. Along with the St. Pete Pier spot is the Sanibel Island flagship location and a waterfront location on Fort Myers Beach. The Facebook post and Rickards said the other Doc Ford’s are not undergoing the name change.
Dedicated visitors of the Jungle Terrace restaurant will face a week-long pause before some of their menu favorites return under the new name.
8790 Bay Pines Blvd., St. Petersburg, 727-290-9578, docfords.com/jungle-terrace/ .
